COMMUNI UR AES WILLIAM SHER 


February 24, 1967. 5 


The Montreal YMCA's annual subscription campaign has to date raised 
$202,500 in its drive for funds to help support increasingly urgent 


youth programs. 


The sum is equal to 63.2% of the $320,000 needed, said J.W. McGiffin, 


president of Canada Steamship Lines and general campaign chairman. 


A number of the Montreal Y's main objectives were capsuled recently 
by Maurice F. Strong, head of Canada's External Aid Program and 


president of the National Council of YMCAs. 


"One of the greatest challenges of our times," he emphasized, "is to 
create a dynamic and flexible institutionalism which enables individuals 


to develop and express the best in themselves, rather than the cumbersome 


and stereotyped bureaucracy which smothers." 
Continued 


February 24, 1967. 


The Montreal YMCA's annual subscription campaign has to date raised 
$202,500 in its drive for funds to help support increasingly urgent 


youth programs. 


The sum is equal to 63.2% of the $320,000 needed, said J.W. McGiffin, 


president of Canada Steamship Lines and general campaign chairman. 


A number of the Montreal Y's main objectives were capsuled recently 
by Maurice F. Strong, head of Canada's External Aid Program and 


president of the National Council of YMCAs. 


"One of the greatest challenges of our times," he emphasized, "is to 
create a dynamic and flexible institutionalism which enables individuals 


to develop and express the best in themselves, rather than the cumbersome 


and stereotyped bureaucracy which smothers." 
Continued 


He pointed out that society is increasingly being lived within and 


affected by larger and more complex institutions. 


"We are educated by big institutions, we work in the big institutions 
of business life or government bureaucracy; many of our needs are 
provided by big institutions and much of our recreational and leisure 


time activities are carried on within an institutional environment." 


Growing Government involvement in specialized aspects of education, 
social welfare and recreation is modifying the need for many services 


formerly offered only by churches and voluntary organizations. 


In many instances, however, this provides voluntary agencies with 
opportunities to increase their effectiveness by becoming the instruments 
through which Government resources are directed and applied. 


Continued 


The YMCA, for example should continue to pioneer research into more 
effective ways of working with youth towards co-operative solutions to 


contemporary problems. 


Helping people adjust to the fact that skills learned during their youth 
may not be sufficient to enable them to earn a livelihood throughout their 


lifetimes should remain another important YMCA objective. 


This the Y can help achieve through its programs of continuing education 
which, while strengthening an individual's ability to understand and cope 


with change, also expand his capacity to enjoy more things more fully. 


Mr. Strong also considers the current confrontation of Canada's two main 
ethnic groups, which he describes as the "greatest challenge ever to 


Canadian nationhood," as another area for Y service. 


"We must become a medium through which English-speaking and French-speaking 
people develop significant meaningful communication with each other," he 


urged."
